sections.html:
Find Lewiston on the Androscoggin River's east bank in Androscoggin County, about midway between Augusta and Portland. Across the water is Auburn, its twin. Roughly 34 of the city's 35.5 square miles are land, and Maine Turnpike access suits buyers who commute out of town.

The 2020 census recorded 37,121 people living in 16,579 housing units, 7.8 percent of them empty. Growth since then has been slow, with 38,866 residents estimated in July 2025.

Textile-mill wealth built most of the older stock: multi-family blocks, three-deckers and small wood-frame houses on narrow lots, many a hundred years old or more. Owners of those should plan for buyer questions on the roof, knob-and-tube wiring, heating and lead paint, with repair quotes pulling the price down.

  • Older wood-frame houses near downtown often have mixed upgrades from different decades.
  • Buildings with three or more units have to register as rentals, as covered below.
  • Condition varies block by block, so a street-level view matters more than a citywide average.

sections.h2: What a Maine winter does to a Lewiston house
sections.html:
The heating system and the roof take the load here. After a hard season, inspectors and buyers check a short list:

  • Ice dams at roof edges, plus attic insulation and ventilation.
  • Oil tank age and location, and whether the furnace or boiler has been serviced.
  • Frost damage to foundations, porch footings and chimneys.
  • Basement moisture, since the city sits beside a river and spring melt raises the water table.

Deferred work on any of these often stalls a regular sale once the inspection report arrives, and it pushes many owners toward an as-is cash buyer.

sections.h2: Lewiston property tax and the revaluation
sections.html:
With a mil rate above $30 and a revaluation underway, tax comes up in nearly every Lewiston sale. Rates below are per $1,000 of assessed value.

Lewiston mil rates by fiscal year
Fiscal yearMil rate per $1,000
2025$31.77
2026$32.78
2027$34.15

The last citywide revaluation took effect in 1988. The state found Lewiston's assessments too low compared with sales, so the city hired Tyler Technologies of Yarmouth to redo them. The new values reflect fair market value as of April 1, 2026, and they will be implemented for the 2027 tax year, which is fiscal 2028.

Your present bill rests on old values, so a buyer will weigh the new value too, not just the bill you hand over.

The assessing and treasury offices share the address 27 Pine Street. Assessor: 207-513-3122, open Monday, Wednesday and Thursday 7:45 AM to 4 PM and Tuesday 7:45 AM to 5:30 PM, closed Friday. Treasury: 207-513-3131, Monday to Friday 8:30 AM to 4 PM. Ask the Assessor what the new value will be for your parcel and bring that number to your first conversation with a buyer.

sections.h2: What happens if property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax in Maine can end in an automatic foreclosure, but the timeline is slow enough that selling usually solves it. First comes a 30-day demand notice, which 36 M.R.S. section 942 allows the collector to send anywhere from 8 months to a year after commitment. If nothing is paid, a lien certificate gets recorded at the registry of deeds.

That recorded lien acts like a mortgage and outranks the others. Under section 943, a lien that sits 18 months without payment of tax, interest and costs is treated as foreclosed, and the owner loses the right to redeem. The treasurer has to warn the owner 30 to 45 days ahead.

  • A closing during the redemption period clears the lien out of your proceeds.
  • A seller who paid a pro rata share under a written proration agreement can have the treasurer record a certificate saying so.
  • A primary residence may qualify for hardship abatement under 36 M.R.S. section 841(2), and a written decision is due within 30 days.

If you believe a value is wrong or illegal, a written abatement request is due within 185 days of commitment. Do not sit on it.

Each side pays half of Maine's transfer tax, which totals $2.20 for every $500 of value. On sales up to $1 million that means $1.10 per $500 apiece. A surcharge of $3.80 per $500 applies to the slice above $1 million on transfers from November 1, 2025 onward, which seldom touches a Lewiston house.

A deed costs $40 to record for most filers. File the deed with a transfer tax declaration at the county registry, naming any exemption you claim. Maine Revenue Services posts the rules.

At the closing table, the title company subtracts your mortgage payoff, any unpaid property tax and your half of the transfer tax from the price. Ask for a draft settlement statement a few days ahead so every figure is familiar before you sign, and bring the deed and a photo ID.

sections.h2: Do Lewiston landlords and sellers of rentals need to register?
sections.html:
Yes, once a building holds three or more units. An owner who lives in one of the units still has to register, while a two-unit building is left out. No fee is charged. Skipping registration risks civil penalties and makes the building ineligible for city loans or grants.

A new multi-family building registers within 30 days after its certificate of occupancy. The City Clerk, at 207-513-3124, can confirm current wording.

Planning and Code Enforcement, 207-513-3125, applies the Maine Uniform Building and Energy Code, in force locally since September 28, 2011. Close out open permits and unfinished work before you list, since a buyer's attorney will look for them.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a house fast in Lewiston
sections.html:
Three paths exist: list, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer. Time and price pull in opposite directions. A house in good order may net more on the market, but showings, inspection negotiation and a buyer's mortgage stretch the timeline. A sale by owner skips the commission and leaves marketing and contracts to you.

With a cash buyer such as us, repairs and financing drop out of the picture. We purchase as-is, which lets a Lewiston house with a worn roof, a tenant or a lien still close. Our offer will sit below a polished retail sale, so measure it against your net once repairs, commission and carrying costs come off.

  • Call the Treasury office first to learn what you owe.
  • Pull together the deed, a mortgage payoff and tenant details if any.
  • Get the offer in writing and see who covers each closing cost.

Any offer, ours included, is yours to refuse. Taking a week to compare two or three options costs little next to choosing the wrong one.

faqs.q: How much is the Lewiston tax rate?
faqs.a: Fiscal 2027 sits at $34.15 per $1,000 of assessed value, after $32.78 in fiscal 2026 and $31.77 in fiscal 2025.

faqs.q: When do new Lewiston property values take effect?
faqs.a: They start with the 2027 tax year, which is fiscal 2028, and reflect fair market value as of April 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lewiston house with unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing pays off the tax, interest and lien costs from your proceeds. A recorded lien that stays unpaid for 18 months is treated as foreclosed, so acting sooner leaves more choices.

faqs.q: Who pays the Maine transfer tax?
faqs.a: Both sides share it equally at $2.20 per $500 of value. Transfers from November 1, 2025 add $3.80 per $500 on the part above $1 million.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a Lewiston duplex as a rental?
faqs.a: No. The duty starts at three units. A call to the City Clerk will confirm current wording.
